<a name="passkey"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Passkey

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Passkey extends \stdClass
```

Source: [framework/core/Passkey.php:34](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Passkey.php#L34)

Passkey wraps lbuchs/webauthn (MIT, no dependencies besides ext-openssl). The browser side is
public/js/services/passkey.js (PasskeyClient.create() / PasskeyClient.get()).

Registration (logged-in user):  registrationOptions($id, $username) -&gt; navigator.credentials.create() -&gt; register($response, $id)
Authentication:                  authenticationOptions([$id])        -&gt; navigator.credentials.get()    -&gt; authenticate($response) returns the user id

The challenge of each ceremony is kept in the session: single use, it expires after $timeout seconds.
Relying party: PASSKEY_RP_ID (the domain, ex: example.com) and PASSKEY_ORIGIN (ex: https://www.example.com) in .env.
Without them the request host is used, which is fine in development: set both in production.
Passkeys need https, except on localhost.

Table (see the face login recipe / wiki 9.9.2):

```
passkeys (id, user_id, credential_id, public_key, sign_count, name, transports, aaguid, created_at, last_used_at)
```

### Constants

+ `SESSION_KEY = '__passkey_challenge'`

### Public properties

+ `public $timeout = 120`
+ `public $userVerification = 'required'`
+ `public $residentKey = 'required'`

<a name="facelogin"></a>
## class Caligrafy\FaceLogin

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class FaceLogin extends \stdClass
```

Source: [framework/core/FaceLogin.php:30](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/FaceLogin.php#L30)

Face login checks used with FaceDetector.liveness() (public/js/services/detect.js)

1. challenge($username) issues a nonce and $count of the CHALLENGES in a random order, kept in the session
2. the browser runs detector.liveness({ challenges }) and posts { nonce, liveness, prints }
3. verify($response, $username) consumes the nonce (single use, short lived) and checks the liveness result and the prints: enough of them, consistent with each other (same face) and not identical (a replayed static print)
4. match($prints, $enrolled) finds the account whose enrolled prints are close to every print

Face prints are computed in the browser: these checks stop photos, naive replays and stolen requests, they do not
stop a determined attacker who controls the browser. Use a passkey (Caligrafy\Passkey) for sensitive accounts.

Distances are euclidean between 128-number face-api descriptors: same person usually &lt; 0.5, others &gt; 0.6

### Constants

+ `SESSION_KEY = '__face_challenge'`
+ `CHALLENGES =['turn-left', 'turn-right', 'smile']`

### Public properties

+ `public static $match = 0.5`
+ `public static $spread = 0.6`
+ `public static $distinct = 0.001`
+ `public static $minPrints = 3`
+ `public static $maxPrints = 12`
+ `public static $count = 2`
+ `public static $ttl = 60`
+ `public static $clock = null`

### Methods

+ [`FaceLogin::challenge()`](#facelogin-challenge)
+ [`FaceLogin::consume()`](#facelogin-consume)
+ [`FaceLogin::verify()`](#facelogin-verify)
